body:
### Problem

I would like to customize the target that native `gx` opens, without replacing its link discovery, visual-selection handling, or launcher/error handling.

My concrete use case is translating Git transport URLs into browser URLs for known hosts, for example:

```text
git://github.com/example/repo.git       -> https://github.com/example/repo
ssh://git@github.com/example/repo.git   -> https://github.com/example/repo
git@github.com:example/repo.git         -> https://github.com/example/repo
```

These illustrate transformations of an **already-resolved target**. Improving detection of SCP-style remotes or other plain-text URLs is a separate concern and not part of this request. These conversion rules are also host-specific policy, not something I am asking Neovim to hard-code.

In Neovim 0.12.5, native normal-mode `gx` already combines LSP document links, URL extmarks, Tree-sitter link metadata, and a `<cfile>` fallback through `vim.ui._get_urls()`. It then passes the target to `vim.ui.open()`. Native visual-mode `gx` extracts the selection and uses the same opener.

The available approaches appear to be:

1. Replace `gx` (or create another mapping), call the private `vim.ui._get_urls()` helper, and reproduce the surrounding normal/visual opening logic just to insert a transformation step.
2. Wrap `vim.ui.open()`. This works for global transformations, but affects all callers and does not receive an explicit indication that the call originated from normal/visual `gx`. I would prefer to scope this policy to `gx`, leaving unrelated opening actions unchanged.

I am not claiming this is impossible with existing Lua configuration; the request is for a documented, narrower extension point that avoids depending on private discovery APIs or duplicating native command behavior.

### Expected behavior

Provide an optional, documented target-transformation hook in the native `gx` path:

```text
native discovery / visual selection
              |
     optional target transformation
              |
      existing vim.ui.open(target)
```

The hook would receive the resolved target and return the target to open. It should run after native extraction and before launching, in both normal and visual mode; when normal-mode discovery returns multiple targets, it should run for each target. Optional context identifying the originating action/mode could be useful, but the exact API name, placement, and signature are open to discussion.

Desired properties:

- With no hook configured, existing `gx` behavior is unchanged.
- Native discovery continues to work, including opening a Markdown link from its label.
- Native selection handling and launcher/error reporting remain reusable rather than copied into user configuration or plugins.
- The transformation does not edit buffer contents.
- Scheme/host-specific conversion rules stay in user configuration or plugins. Core does not need to know about GitHub, SSH-to-web host mappings, or `.git` suffix conventions.
- Unrelated `vim.ui.open()` callers are unaffected unless explicitly opting into the same mechanism.

An existing public mechanism that supports this scoped use case would also solve the problem; I would appreciate guidance if I have missed one.

Related: #23231 introduced the native, netrw-independent opening approach. This proposal is a small customization point around that behavior, not a request for another browser launcher or a Git-specific link-opening engine.

milestone.description: We don't plan to work on this, but will accept high quality contributions from someone who will own the feature and follow up on bug reports.
milestone.title: needs-owner

title: gx: add a target-transformation hook before vim.ui.open()
